newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi lawyer says jailed British nurses see kin.
newsitem.headline: Saudi lawyer says jailed British nurses see kin.

text.p: A lawyer for two British nurses charged with murder in Saudi Arabia said on Tuesday the women had received visits from their families over the weekend and were in good spiritis.
Saudi Lawyer Salah al-Hejailan said he had also met with the families of Deborah Parry, 41 and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, to discuss legal strategy and said the relatives were relaxed and confident.
"The families were in the (Eastern Saudi city of) Dammam and saw the girls on Saturday, Sunday and Monday," he told Reuters at his villa in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
"I met with the families on Thursday in this salon and we revised everything together," he said, gesturing at the white rattan furniture in a flowery lounge.

The two women have been charged with the murder of Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55, in her dormitory room at the King Fahd medical complex in the oil-rich city of Dhahran on December 11. She had been stabbed, bludgeoned with a hammer and suffocated.
If convicted guilty and sentenced to death, the two women could face public beheading by the sword -- the first time Western women had been executed in conservative Islamic kingdom.
Gilford's family in Australia have ruled out a clemency appeal, saying the two should face the maximum punishment.
Hejailan said the two women were being treated well and were in high spirits.
"They feel they are up to defending themselves," he said.
The U.S.-educated lawyer said his colleagues frequently went to the women's prison in Damman to visit Parry and McLauchlan.
"British lawyers from my office see them every 10 days or so," he said.
Legal experts said that if they were found guilty of manslaughter rather than murder the nurses would not be condemned to death.
Saudi police said the nurses confessed to the murder and the confessions had been filed with three judges.
But Hejailan's firm said the women had withdrawn their confessions, and one of them retracted a statement that she had a lesbian relationship with the victim.
The lawyer said he had discussed a new strategy with the suspects, but declined to say what the fresh approach entailed.
No trial date has yet been set, he added.
